name: The Icicle Works
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: A Liverpool trio named after a Frederik Pohl story put "Birds Fly (Whisper to a Scream)" into the American top 40, then watched their US label turn down the next album.

hero.by: The Icicle Works at the Patronaat, Haarlem, May 17, 1987. Photo: Fotoburo De Boer, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: From the cabaret circuit to a sci-fi name
eras.text: Ian McNabb had spent his teens in cabaret groups playing working men's clubs. In 1980 he put together a trio with tribal drums and a string machine, and named it after a science fiction story.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Icicle Works · Wikipedia: Ian McNabb · The Electricity Club
years.h: Chris Layhe answers 20-year-old Ian McNabb's ad
years.p: Layhe became bassist and co-writer; [[Chris Sharrock|3bb8485e-eea9-4db7-9027-141ee4a85b83]], McNabb's friend from teenage cabaret group Young World, took the drums. The name came from Frederik Pohl's story "The Day the Icicle Works Closed".
years.xp:
McNabb's cabaret groups had failed auditions for Opportunity Knocks and New Faces. He quit City Lights in February 1980 after agreeing to start a band with Sharrock.

He played keyboards from the first rehearsal: a Korg 770 and a Logan string machine bought in 1977. "I couldn't afford a Moog," he told The Electricity Club.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Icicle Works · Wikipedia: Ian McNabb
years.h: A six-song cassette called Ascending
years.p: The band's first release was self-issued. The same year McNabb auditioned for the part of Barry Grant in Brookside and didn't get it.

yt: "Nirvana" live in Sefton Park for The Old Grey Whistle Test
years.h: "Nirvana" reaches No. 15 on the UK indie chart
years.p: An independent single, released a year before Beggars Banquet signed them.

eras.title: Whisper to a scream
eras.text: Beggars Banquet signed them, John Peel played them, and a Rickenbacker 12-string and a brass intro put them in the UK top 20. In America a remixed, retitled single went top 40.

years.src: Wikipedia: Birds Fly · The Electricity Club
years.h: "Birds Fly (Whisper to a Scream)" on Situation Two
years.p: [[Hugh Jones|d62cacb0-f4ef-4d77-9d7d-86232507ff1a]] produced it, a woman named only as Mariella speaks the intro, and [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] played both sides. It went to No. 2 on the indie chart and No. 89 nationally.

years.cap: Ian McNabb, Chris Layhe and Chris Sharrock, c. 1984
years.src: The Electricity Club · WriteWyattUK · Wikipedia: The Icicle Works (album)
years.h: "Love Is a Wonderful Colour" climbs to No. 15
years.p: After a December of airplay it peaked in January, the band's only UK top 20 hit. McNabb calls it "a long, slow burn".
years.xp: WriteWyattUK describes the brassy intro and McNabb's Byrds-style Rickenbacker 12-string. Pitchfork later called it one of those tracks that make you think there's something left in 80s crate-digging.

years.src: The Quietus · The Electricity Club · Wikipedia: The Icicle Works (album)
years.h: The debut, sung over a bowl of menthol steam
years.p: Hugh Jones spent days mixing single tracks; McNabb remembers losing his voice. It reached No. 24 in the UK and No. 40 in the US.
years.xp: "I hated it when it came out... too clean, not dangerous enough," McNabb told The Quietus decades later, though he now says every song on it is good. To The Electricity Club he called Jones "such a taskmaster".

years.cap: The original trio in a Beggars Banquet press photo, c. 1984
years.h: Arista flips the title and drops the "The"
years.p: For America, "Whisper to a Scream (Birds Fly)" lost Mariella's intro and the band became Icicle Works. It reached No. 37 on the Hot 100 and No. 19 in Canada.

years.h: "Hollow Horse" misses the UK chart
years.p: The UK-only follow-up flopped, and "All the Daughters" and "Seven Horses" followed it. Chris "Tugsie" Turrill joined the live band on keyboards.

years.h: Live on The Tube
years.p: The trio played Channel 4's The Tube in Newcastle.

eras.title: Rejected as punk-rock demos
eras.text: The second album was denser and louder, and British critics loved it. Arista wouldn't release it in America, and the American career stopped there.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Small Price of a Bicycle · The Big Takeover
years.h: Arista won't release The Small Price of a Bicycle
years.p: That was Arista's verdict on the second album, which never came out in the US or Canada. In Britain it reached No. 55, and Sounds gave it five stars.
years.xp:
"The record company rejected our second album because it didn't sound like they thought it needed to sound," McNabb told The Big Takeover. He says the US label also wouldn't release "Love Is a Wonderful Colour" there, and that killed the band's momentum.

In Canada, Vertigo put out a five-track EP, Seven Horses Deep, instead.

years.cap: The band as a four-piece, c. 1986
yt: "Who Do You Want for Your Love" video
years.h: Dave Green takes over keyboards; Seven Singles Deep charts
years.p: Green replaced Turrill live and began playing on the records. Beggars collected the 12-inch mixes on a UK-only LP that reached No. 52.

years.h: "Understanding Jane" reaches No. 52
years.p: The first of three singles, with "Who Do You Want for Your Love" and "Evangeline", that all stalled in the low 50s.

eras.title: Broudie, then Blind
eras.text: Ian Broudie produced the third album and the band toured hard, including the Netherlands and American college radio. By 1988 McNabb was producing himself, and the original trio was coming apart.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Icicle Works · Wikipedia: If You Want to Defeat Your Enemy Sing His Song
years.h: [[Ian Broudie|45154afb-9a09-41bf-a39c-654c3f497c08]] produces the third album
years.p: It reached No. 28 in the UK and was released in North America too. "Evangeline" came out as a single that January.
play: If You Want to Defeat Your Enemy Sing His Song

years.cap: With DJ Steve Masters at Live 105, San Francisco, January 1987
years.src: Wikimedia Commons: Icicle Works at Live 105
years.h: Live 105 in San Francisco has them in the studio
years.p: The band visited DJ Steve Masters at the Bay Area alternative station.

years.src: Wikimedia Commons: Icicle Works, Patronaat Haarlem · Wikipedia: If You Want to Defeat Your Enemy Sing His Song
years.h: On stage at the Patronaat in Haarlem
years.p: A Dutch club date on the 1987 tour. A 1986 London show from the same period came out later as Live at the Town and Country Club.

years.h: "High Time" stalls at No. 76, then goes to No. 13 in America
years.p: The 1987 single did better in 1988 on Billboard's new Modern Rock chart.

years.h: McNabb produces Blind himself
years.p: The last album by the original line-up reached No. 40. The US release had a different cover and track list.

years.big: A few grand for one, a few hundred for the others
q: I pretty much told them what to do. It wasn't really a band.
years.src: The Quietus · WriteWyattUK · Wikipedia: The Icicle Works · Wikipedia: Chris Sharrock
years.h: Sharrock leaves for the La's, Layhe goes too, and Beggars drops the band
years.p: [[Chris Sharrock|3bb8485e-eea9-4db7-9027-141ee4a85b83]] went off to drum on The La's' "There She Goes". McNabb says the money gap and settling down did the rest.
years.xp:
"I'd get a few grand and they'd get a few hundred. People have got families and bills to pay," McNabb told The Quietus. He told WriteWyattUK, "I felt our time had passed."

Sharrock went on to The Wild Swans, World Party, [[The Lightning Seeds|1ba601a0-3401-4b28-8ddd-9af8203661e8]], Robbie Williams' band, [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]], [[Beady Eye|a0e10984-0eca-4920-a171-5fd7a62ee069]] and Noel Gallagher's High Flying Birds. Layhe later ran events at Liverpool's Bluecoat arts centre and taught guitar.

eras.title: The brand name
eras.text: McNabb carried on with a changing cast and a new label that wanted the old name on the sleeve. The record flopped and the name was put away.

years.h: Zak Starkey takes the drum stool
years.p: [[Zak Starkey|fa6d1fab-dc90-4e76-bdf9-28e06d1010ff]] played drums for a time as McNabb rebuilt the band. Dave Green became a full member and left within the year.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Icicle Works · The Quietus
years.h: Permanent Damage, a solo album with the band's name on it
years.p: Epic's Muff Winwood wanted a brand he knew. Roy Corkill played bass and ex-10cc drummer Paul Burgess drums. It failed to chart and Epic dropped them.
years.xp: "A Pink Floyd record will sell a lot more than a Roger Waters one. So I was blinded by money and it was a mistake," McNabb told The Quietus.

years.h: McNabb goes solo, and later records with Crazy Horse
years.p: "Great Dreams of Heaven" was his first solo single. His second album, Head Like a Rock, with Crazy Horse's Ralph Molina and Billy Talbot, made the 1994 Mercury Prize shortlist.

eras.title: The name comes back out
eras.text: After fifteen years solo, McNabb brought the name back for anniversary tours with his solo band. In 2024 a founding member came back for the first time.

years.h: Six UK shows mark 25 years
years.p: McNabb, bassist Roy Corkill, keyboardist Richard Naiff and drummer Mathew Priest, the core of McNabb's solo band.

years.h: Thirtieth-anniversary shows after a three-year break
years.p: "I'm not afraid of my past, like some are," McNabb said of the two-hour sets drawn from all five albums.

years.cap: Ian McNabb at the Brudenell Social Club, Leeds
years.h: Two and a half hours for the 35th anniversary
years.p: The tour mixed band and solo songs, with McNabb on a Micro Mellotron.

years.h: Chris Layhe rejoins for acoustic shows
years.p: The original bassist was back on stage with McNabb for the first time since 1988.
